# polygons.library: RemoveDuplicateVertices

**Tier:** `geometry`. **File:** [polygons.library](../polygons.library.md). **Source:** [stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato, line 630](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato#L630).

Copied from source, comments included. A comment records intent. The body is the algorithm. Neither is a proof that the result is correct. Names resolve in the whole compilation.

This slice: RemoveDuplicateVertices, RemoveCollinearVertices, Canonical, RingsAreDisjoint, IsSimple, HolesLieInside, Canonical.

```plato

    // The polygon with repeated vertices dropped. Does NOT make a polygon simple —
    // crossings are untouched — it removes the degeneracies that are removable without
    // changing the region.
    RemoveDuplicateVertices(p: Polygon2D): Polygon2D
        => Polygon2D(p.Points.RingWithoutDuplicateVertices);

    // The polygon with collinear midpoints and spike tips dropped.
    RemoveCollinearVertices(p: Polygon2D): Polygon2D
        => Polygon2D(p.Points.RingWithoutCollinearVertices);

    // The polygon in canonical form: no repeated vertices, no collinear midpoints,
    // counter-clockwise. Area-preserving, so it is safe to apply to any input; it does
    // not repair a self-intersecting ring, which cannot be repaired without changing
    // the region it describes.
    Canonical(p: Polygon2D): Polygon2D
        => Polygon2D(p.Points.RingWithoutDuplicateVertices
            .RingWithoutCollinearVertices.CounterClockwiseRing);

    //==
    // # PolygonWithHoles2D predicates

    // True when no edge of either ring meets an edge of the other.
    RingsAreDisjoint(a: Array<Point2D>, b: Array<Point2D>): Boolean
        => a.Count.Range.Any(i => b.Count.Range.Any(j =>
            SegmentsIntersect(a[i], a.AtModulo(i + 1), b[j], b.AtModulo(j + 1)))).Not;

    // True when every ring of the region is simple and no two of them meet — the
    // structural half of the declaration's invariants. The other half, that the holes
    // lie inside the boundary, is `HolesLieInside`.
    IsSimple(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Boolean
        => r.Boundary.IsSimple
        && r.Holes.All(h => h.IsSimple)
        && r.Holes.All(h => RingsAreDisjoint(r.Boundary.Points, h.Points))
        && r.Holes.Count.Range.All(i => r.Holes.Count.Range.All(j =>
            j > i ? RingsAreDisjoint(r.Holes[i].Points, r.Holes[j].Points) : true));

    // True when every hole lies inside the boundary. Exact only for a region that is
    // already `IsSimple`: given that no ring crosses another, a single vertex decides
    // the whole hole, so the even-odd test on one vertex is enough.
    HolesLieInside(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Boolean
        => r.Holes.All(h => r.Boundary.Contains(h.Points.First));

    // The region in canonical form: every ring cleaned, the boundary counter-clockwise
    // and every hole clockwise, which is the winding the declaration states and the
    // triangulator assumes.
    Canonical(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): PolygonWithHoles2D
        => (r.Boundary.Canonical,
            r.Holes.Map(h => Polygon2D(h.Canonical.Points.ReversedRing)));
}
```
